audit.whatIsWrong: EVEN at 6/10 sits oddly against 60.47% Emerald+, though only over 43 games.
audit.why: 60% is a strongly favoured lane; the sample is small enough that I would not swing the rating far, but EVEN is the wrong label.
audit.corrected: Favoured, nearer 5/10, flagged as a small-sample read.

audit.whatIsWrong: The chart gives Maokai Levels 2 and 3 while spikes[0] on the same page describes the level 2-3 poke war as Aurora's to start and win.
audit.why: Twisted Advance reaches 525 and Bramble Smash 600; Twofold Hex is 900. Before he can close, the poke war is one-sided.
audit.corrected: Levels 2 and 3 should read Aurora, matching the spike text.

audit.whatIsWrong: The most important interaction in the matchup is missing and the page currently implies its opposite. Sap Magic's cooldown is reduced every time Maokai is STRUCK BY AN ENEMY SPELL — so poking him is what powers his healing. The page instead tells you your passive wins the HP race.
audit.why: Riot's text: 'Each time Maokai casts a spell or is struck by an enemy's spell, this cooldown is reduced.'
audit.corrected: Every Twofold Hex you land charges his Sap Magic heal. Poke to set up a kill, not to grind him down, and have Grievous Wounds before you try to finish.

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[1] says that if you drop the rift and he is outside it, he cannot target Twisted Advance onto you. Between Worlds confers no such protection.
audit.why: Between Worlds damages, slows enemies inside the area, and lets Aurora teleport across it. It does not block targeting.
audit.corrected: The rift helps by slowing him inside it and letting you cross as he commits — it does not stop the root being aimed at you.

audit.whatIsWrong: Twisted Advance makes Maokai UNTARGETABLE for the duration of the dash, so burst spent as he flies in is thrown away. Never stated.
audit.why: Riot's text: 'Maokai contorts into a mass of moving roots, becoming untargetable and dashing to the target.' Confirmed independently by champ-data/_kits/_missing/aurora.json.
audit.corrected: Hold your damage until he lands — while the roots are travelling he cannot be hit at all.

audit.whatIsWrong: No numbers. Twisted Advance is 14s at rank 1 against your 22s leap — he roots more often than you can escape.
audit.why: Maokai Q 7s, W 14s, E 18s, R 130/110/90; Aurora W 22s at rank 1.
audit.corrected: Twisted Advance 14s versus Across the Veil 22s; Nature's Grasp 130s at rank 1.

edits.before: W-blink his root — build MR, poke him. Aurora wins the Twisted Advance cooldown windows.
edits.after: Your poke charges his Sap Magic heal — W-blink the root, and buy anti-heal early.

edits.before: Between the Worlds zones the whole all-in — fights inside it are yours. Reassess every all-in at 6 — Maokai's ultimate changes the math too.
edits.after: Hold damage while Twisted Advance flies — he is untargetable in the dash. Nature's Grasp is 130s at rank 1, so punish the miss hard.

edits.before: Between the Worlds zones the whole all-in — build your teamfight around that. Maokai carry threat: 7/10 — anti-heal stays core, shift to picks and wave control if he gets ahead.
edits.after: Between Worlds slows and splits the fight — build your teamfight around that. Maokai carry threat: 7/10 — anti-heal stays core against Sap Magic, shift to picks if he gets ahead.

edits.after: - Maokai Twisted Advance: 14s at rank 1 versus your 22s leap, and he is untargetable during the dash — hold damage until he lands. - Sap Magic's heal charges every time your spell hits him. - Nature's Grasp: 130s.

edits.after: Burning damage into Twisted Advance mid-dash — he is untargetable until he arrives, so all of it is wasted.

edits.before: Between Worlds is the answer to his W: if you drop the rift and he's outside it he can't target his Twisted Advance dash-root onto you — walk through it and all-in once your passive has won the HP race.

notes: The Sap Magic finding inverts advice that is currently on the page: spikes[1] tells you to all-in 'once your passive has won the HP race', but chip poke is exactly what accelerates his heal. I rewrote that line. Small sample warning on the 60.47% figure — 43 games. The 'untargetable' rewrite is part of the champion-wide problem (61 occurrences in champ-data/content/aurora.js), but note the direction reverses here: Maokai genuinely does go untargetable, Aurora does not.
